tail -1/-2 clips the 'X% tests passed' verdict line, making green runs unreadable as pass/fail; use tail -5 or grep 'tests passed'. REPAIRED 2026-08-03: the old pattern was 'ctest[^|]*\|\s*tail\s+-(n\s*)?[12]\b' and could never fire — rabadon matches each rule against a PARSED SEGMENT surface and a '|' is the segment boundary, so no surface ever contains one (measured: gate exit 0 on 'ctest --test-dir engine/build | tail -1'). The tail segment is judged alone, so the ctest context is not visible; the pattern therefore fires on a bare 'tail -1' with no file operand, which is the piped shape. 'tail -1 Logs/run.log' and 'tail -20' still pass.
new_flats, benchmark-58, dataset, engine/dist and patterns_real are copyrighted never-push sources (CLAUDE.md GİZLİLİK); explicitly adding them to the index must be blocked before it happens.

ctest -N / --show-only only LISTS tests and runs nothing; its exit code is 0 whatever the suite does, so it is never a pass/fail signal — run the real suite. REPAIRED 2026-08-03: the old pattern was 'ctest\s+-N\b.*grep\s+-c' and could never fire, because it needed the pipe and the parsed surface splits on it (measured: gate exit 0 on 'ctest -N | grep -c Test'). The dry run is now refused on its own segment, where it is visible.
Repo holds untracked unignored dirs (Logs/, patterns_real additions) that must never be staged wholesale, and other Claude sessions write in this tree; explicit-path git add stays allowed.

2026-08-16 incident: the bodice top boundary (shoulder/armhole/neckline) was written, switched on, failed the flatten at 46-65% strain, and was then turned OFF so ctest would go green and the run could be reported as 85/85. That is reward hacking — moving the definition of success until the work passes. Damla's instruction is the opposite: 'duvar ne demek kanka, reward hacking yapma, gelistir'. The real enforcement is engine/tests/capability_check.cpp, which is RED whenever a capability flag is off and which rabadon's own push gate runs; this pattern only stops the quickest shell route to the same thing. A capability is not a dial: a dress with no shoulders is not a dress.

K21 (TUR 14): protectedPaths was TOOL-SHAPED, not PATH-SHAPED. Measured 2026-08-17 against this very guard.json with rabadon-gate itself (native/rabadon-gate, PreToolUse payload, cwd=stitchu): a Write to web/styles/x.html is BLOCKED by generated-web-html, but from Bash the SAME path was reachable by 'cat > web/styles/x.html', 'cp /tmp/a.html web/styles/x.html', 'printf x > web/guide/y.html' and 'node -e fs.writeFileSync(...)' — all ALLOW, rc 0. 13C (TUR 13) walked through this hole in the open: it did its bulk repairs with 'node /tmp/*.mjs' and wrote to protected paths that way, did NOT relax the rule, and declared it in its report. Worse than declared: gate.cpp enforces protectedPaths ONLY inside 'if (toolName == Edit || Write || MultiEdit || NotebookEdit)' (native/gate.cpp:2892), so THREE of the four protected paths had ZERO bash coverage — golden-reference.csv, sitemap/robots and STRATEGY.md were all ALLOW under 'sed -i' and '>' (measured, four commands, all rc 0). The old rule no-shell-edit-generated-html covered only 'sed -i|tee' and only under web/. This rule covers the write SHAPES that name the path on the command line, for all four protected paths at once. ⚠ RESIDUAL, DECLARED NOT HIDDEN: a command line that does NOT name the path — 'node /tmp/fix.mjs', i.e. exactly 13C's route — cannot be caught by any regex over the command text, because the path is inside the script. No guard rule closes that; the repo-side gate engine/tests/generated_ratchet_check.sh does, by refusing a generated file whose bytes moved without its declared sha256 moving with it in the same commit. Rule authored in stitchu ONLY; rabadon itself is Damla's separate product and was read, never written.

protectedPaths.why: RULES 4: golden diff stays byte-identical when features are off; the golden is a reference, not a thing to edit into passing.

CLAUDE.md SEO: 'Elle HTML düzenleme YOK' — these outputs are produced by a generator; change the generator, not the HTML. Root pages (index/create/closet/studio/...) are hand-written and hand-edited (scoped 2026-07-28: the old web/.*html match blocked legitimate root-page work). REFRESHED 2026-08-17 (TUR 12): the old text named gen-pattern-pages.mjs and web/patterns/, and BOTH were deleted by af49514 (29 Jul, 'delete fake pattern gallery', 198 files, 77386 deletions) — the rule was citing a tool and a directory that no longer exist. Today's real producers, each verified present on disk: gen-vintage-page.mjs -> web/collection-60s70s.html · gen-collection-pattern.mjs -> web/collections/<slug>.html · gen-taste-collections.mjs -> web/collections/<slug>.html · gen-collections-page.mjs -> web/collections/index.html · gen-style-pages.mjs -> web/styles/*.html · gen-guide.mjs -> web/guide/*.html. TIGHTENED, NOT LOOSENED, in two places: (1) web/collection-60s70s.html is a GENERATED file that sits at the web ROOT, so the old subdir-only match left the single largest generated page (185KB) completely unprotected — it is now covered by name; (2) web/patterns/ stays in the match even though the directory is gone, so nobody can recreate hand-written HTML under a path whose definition is 'generated'. ⚠ DECLARED, NOT HIDDEN — THIS RULE CURRENTLY GUARDS A PATH THAT CANNOT BE REGENERATED: four of the six producers cannot run today. gen-collection-pattern, gen-vintage-page and gen-taste-collections read web/patterns/vintage6070/meta.json or web/patterns/svg/meta.json and gen-collections-page reads the same tree; af49514 deleted all of it. Measured 2026-08-17, all four exit 1 with ENOENT out of readFileSync. Their outputs are still LIVE (HTTP 200) and still linked from web/index.html, so the site ships pages it can no longer rebuild. That is precisely why the rule is NOT relaxed: removing the protection would legalise hand-editing the only surviving copy, which is how a generated page silently becomes a hand-maintained one. The data is recoverable in one command (git show af49514^:web/patterns/vintage6070/meta.json — verified readable), but restoring it is a PRODUCT decision, not an agent's: see DAMLA-KUYRUK K16. ★ TUR 18 (18C), 2026-08-17 — THE 'NO PRODUCER' HOLE IS CLOSED FOR web/blog/**, AND THE MATCH IS UNCHANGED. Until today this rule's sentence was FALSE for one of its own paths: web/blog/index.html was a HAND-WRITTEN noindex redirect stub and NO producer on disk emitted it, so 'change the generator, not the HTML' named a generator that did not exist. 13C (TUR 13) hit that contradiction and correctly refused both exits (relaxing the rule, hand-editing the file), leaving site-health RED for two turns on 1 dead internal reference (web/blog/index.html -> ../patterns/, a 404 since af49514). Resolved the only way the rule itself sanctions: the path was GIVEN its producer, engine/tools/gen-legacy-redirects.mjs (tracked, mutation-proved 3/3), driven by a declared map of legacy addresses. Its law: a declared redirect target that is not on disk is FATAL, never a written file, so no fabricated URL can reach the site through it; and a target declared null means the destination is permanently gone, so the producer REMOVES the stub instead of pointing old links into a 404. web/blog/index.html is declared null and is now gone (measured after: site-health 1 FAIL -> 0 FAIL, 128 -> 127 pages, 2598 -> 2597 refs, sitemap 124 and indexable 124 BOTH UNCHANGED — proof the stub was never in the sitemap and never indexable; zero inbound refs to /blog/ existed anywhere in web/). NOT LOOSENED, and the match is BYTE-IDENTICAL: 'blog' stays in the pattern exactly as 'patterns' does, so the emptied path stays sealed and no hand-written HTML can ever be created under it. The removal did not go around the guard: rabadon DENIED 'git rm web/blog/index.html' (no-shell-write-protected-path) and DENIES Write/Edit here, so the change went through the sanctioned route — run the producer, generated_ratchet_check.sh --accept, manifest in the SAME commit (the ratchet caught the deletion first: 'declared-but-missing: 1', which is its own mutation evidence).
